name: Yamaha P-145BT
img: Yamaha P-145BT 88-key digital piano in black with music rest
verdict: The safest beginner piano at any price: GHC weighted keys, a clean concert-grand sound and Bluetooth audio. Any price under $450 is a good Black Friday buy.
pros: Reliable keys that feel close to an acoustic
Bluetooth audio for lessons and songs
cons: Make sure the listing says P-145BT

name: Roland FP-10
img: Roland FP-10 88-key digital piano in black with small music rest
verdict: The best-feeling keys under $500, the same PHA-4 action as Roland's pricier FP-30X. Under $450, it's the deal I'd jump on for a serious beginner.

name: Kawai ES60
img: Kawai ES60 88-key digital piano in black with music rest
verdict: The best piano sound on this list, from Shigeru Kawai concert grand samples. Its price moves around a lot, so wait for something under $470.

name: Alesis Recital Pro MKII
img: Alesis Recital Pro MKII 88-key digital piano in black
verdict: The cheapest 88 weighted keys I'd still recommend, with a pedal in the box. Fine for occasional players; under $320 it's a very fair price.

name: Roland FP-30X
img: Roland FP-30X 88-key digital piano in black with music rest
verdict: The buy-once pick: the FP-10's PHA-4 keys plus Bluetooth audio, 256-note polyphony and bigger speakers. Worth it if you can get it close to $600.

name: Casio Privia PX-S1100
img: Casio Privia PX-S1100 slim 88-key digital piano in red
verdict: One of the slimmest 88-key weighted pianos you can buy, about 9 inches deep, with Bluetooth through the included adapter. Only a deal well under its usual price.
cons: Touch controls take getting used to
